title: Nvidia and TCV Invest in AI Video Startup Higgsfield
excerpt: The chipmaker and the growth investor joined an extension of Higgsfield's Series B, building on August's $400 million round at a $5.4 billion valuation, as the AI video platform passes 40 million registered users.
body:
• Nvidia and growth investor TCV have invested in Higgsfield, the San Francisco-based AI video startup, in an extension of its Series B round. The size of the extension and its valuation were not disclosed.
  • The extension builds on an August round that raised $400 million at a $5.4 billion valuation, led by DST Global — more than four times Higgsfield's $1.3 billion valuation in January.
  • Higgsfield reports more than 40 million registered users across over 200 countries and an annualized revenue run rate that passed $1 billion in September, up from $200 million in January.
  • The new money is earmarked for global infrastructure and hiring, as demand for AI video generation continues to outrun the company's capacity.

Nvidia and venture firm TCV have put new money into Higgsfield, the AI video generation startup founded by former Snap executive Alex Mashrabov, extending the company's Series B round, according to Bloomberg reporting cited by Startup Fortune and coverage in Variety. Higgsfield, headquartered in San Francisco with most of its engineering team in Kazakhstan, did not disclose the size of the extension or the valuation at which it was struck.

The announcement landed the same day Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was in Kazakhstan as the special guest of a national AI Month event in Astana — his first visit to the country where Higgsfield, co-founded by Mashrabov and Erzat Dulat in 2023, keeps the bulk of its engineers.

The Round Behind the Extension

The base round closed in August, raising $400 million at a $5.4 billion valuation led by DST Global, with Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Intel Capital, Fifth Wall, Tribe Capital, Smash Capital, Valor Capital, Liberty Global Tech Ventures, Mirae Asset Capital and NTT DOCOMO Ventures taking part. That valuation was already more than four times the $1.3 billion mark set in January, when an $80 million extension closed.

https://x.com/fourweekmba/status/2113532271177187839

TCV, which has previously backed Netflix, Spotify and ByteDance, cited Higgsfield's "radically faster, professional-grade and AI-native mechanism for creators, brand marketers and agencies alike to turn ideas into images and video" as its rationale, according to Emergent.

What Higgsfield Does

Higgsfield, available at higgsfield.ai, lets creators and brands generate and edit video and images without a camera or studio. Rather than betting on a single model, the platform aggregates roughly 35 AI video generation engines alongside its own technology, so users can pick different models for storyboarding, character creation, audio generation and final rendering. Its products include the mobile-first Diffuse and the longer-form ReelMagic.

Mashrabov ran generative AI at Snap before co-founding the company. Higgsfield says its annualized revenue run rate surpassed $1 billion in September, up from $200 million in January, and that its registered user base has grown past 40 million people across more than 200 countries. Those are company-reported figures: a revenue run rate is a projection from current performance, not revenue booked over a full year, and registered users are not the same as paying customers.

Why Nvidia Is Buying In

Video generation is one of the most compute-hungry categories in consumer AI: a text-to-video model must render coherent motion across dozens of frames, burning far more compute per request than a chatbot query. Nvidia has spent two years building stakes in application-layer AI companies, not only the infrastructure firms that obviously consume its chips, and it also backed Runway, which raised $315 million at a $5.3 billion valuation in February. China's Kling AI, owned by Kuaishou Technology, raised $2.8 billion at roughly a $15 billion valuation this summer.

For Nvidia, each application stake is also a demand signal — a closer look at where GPU consumption is heading, rather than waiting for cloud providers' quarterly capital spending guidance.

What's Next

Higgsfield plans to use the new capital for global infrastructure and hiring, chasing demand it says is still outrunning its capacity to serve it. The open question the extension does not answer is valuation: with no new price disclosed, the company's next priced round will be the first public test of whether the $5.4 billion August mark still holds.
